# Local Agent Harness (MVP 0.1)

Personal CLI harness using `mlx-code==0.0.42` as the agent runtime.

## Requirements

- macOS on Apple Silicon
- Python 3.12+
- `mlx-code==0.0.42` installed in the Python environment used by this project
- Model downloaded: `mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-OptiQ-4bit`

## Install

Use the same Python environment where `mlx-code` is installed. If you installed it with `uv tool`,
the tool environment is isolated; the project venv will need its own package installation.

```bash
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .
```

## Start the local inference server

Terminal 1:

```bash
mlc --model mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-OptiQ-4bit --leash none
```

Keep this terminal running.

## Start the harness

Terminal 2, from the project directory:

```bash
lah
```

Read-only mode is the default. To enable Write, Edit, and Bash tools:

```bash
lah --write
```

Or toggle in a running session:

```text
/write on
/write off
```

## Commands

```text
/help
/new
/sessions
/resume SESSION_ID
/memory
/remember The API uses FastAPI and SQLAlchemy.
 /search FastAPI
/quit
```

## Persistence model

- Full chat transcript is stored in SQLite after each user turn.
- `/resume SESSION_ID` restores the saved `agent.messages`.
- `/remember TEXT` stores explicit long-term project memory.
- Memory is scoped to the resolved project path.
- SQLite is stored outside the repository in:
  `~/Library/Application Support/LocalAgentHarness/<project-key>/state.sqlite3`

This keeps agent memory even when mlx-code worktrees are cleaned up.

## Important implementation note

This MVP uses the documented `mlx_code.repl.Agent` API:
`Agent(system=..., tool_names=...)`, `agent.run(...)`, and `agent.messages`.

It intentionally keeps the transcript in SQLite rather than relying only on mlx-code's Git checkpoints.
Because the package is installed separately via `uv tool`, make sure the harness Python environment
can import `mlx_code`. If it cannot, install `mlx-code==0.0.42` in the harness venv or use the
same interpreter as the uv tool environment.

## Current limitations

- No automatic summarization/compaction yet.
- Long-term memory is explicitly saved with `/remember`.
- No multi-agent execution.
- No automatic approval prompt around individual shell commands; therefore write mode should be
  enabled only when you trust the task and the project. Read-only mode is the safe default.
- The runtime's worktree behavior should be tested on a disposable Git repository before using
  write mode on important projects.

# Local Agent Harness (MVP 0.1)

Personal CLI harness using `mlx-code==0.0.42` as the agent runtime.

## Requirements

- macOS on Apple Silicon
- Python 3.12+
- `mlx-code==0.0.42` installed in the Python environment used by this project
- Model downloaded: `mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-OptiQ-4bit`

## Install

Use the same Python environment where `mlx-code` is installed. If you installed it with `uv tool`,
the tool environment is isolated; the project venv will need its own package installation.

```bash
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .
```

## Start the local inference server

Terminal 1:

```bash
mlc --model mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-OptiQ-4bit --leash none
```

Keep this terminal running.

## Start the harness

Terminal 2, from the project directory:

```bash
lah
```

Read-only mode is the default. To enable Write, Edit, and Bash tools:

```bash
lah --write
```

Or toggle in a running session:

```text
/write on
/write off
```

## Commands

```text
/help
/new
/sessions
/resume SESSION_ID
/memory
/remember The API uses FastAPI and SQLAlchemy.
 /search FastAPI
/quit
```

## Persistence model

- Full chat transcript is stored in SQLite after each user turn.
- `/resume SESSION_ID` restores the saved `agent.messages`.
- `/remember TEXT` stores explicit long-term project memory.
- Memory is scoped to the resolved project path.
- SQLite is stored outside the repository in:
  `~/Library/Application Support/LocalAgentHarness/<project-key>/state.sqlite3`

This keeps agent memory even when mlx-code worktrees are cleaned up.

## Important implementation note

This MVP uses the documented `mlx_code.repl.Agent` API:
`Agent(system=..., tool_names=...)`, `agent.run(...)`, and `agent.messages`.

It intentionally keeps the transcript in SQLite rather than relying only on mlx-code's Git checkpoints.
Because the package is installed separately via `uv tool`, make sure the harness Python environment
can import `mlx_code`. If it cannot, install `mlx-code==0.0.42` in the harness venv or use the
same interpreter as the uv tool environment.

## Current limitations

- No automatic summarization/compaction yet.
- Long-term memory is explicitly saved with `/remember`.
- No multi-agent execution.
- No automatic approval prompt around individual shell commands; therefore write mode should be
  enabled only when you trust the task and the project. Read-only mode is the safe default.
- The runtime's worktree behavior should be tested on a disposable Git repository before using
  write mode on important projects.

# Local Agent Harness (MVP 0.1)

Personal CLI harness using `mlx-code==0.0.42` as the agent runtime.

## Requirements

- macOS on Apple Silicon
- Python 3.12+
- `mlx-code==0.0.42` installed in the Python environment used by this project
- Model downloaded: `mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-OptiQ-4bit`

## Install

Use the same Python environment where `mlx-code` is installed. If you installed it with `uv tool`,
the tool environment is isolated; the project venv will need its own package installation.

```bash
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .
```

## Start the local inference server

Terminal 1:

```bash
mlc --model mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-OptiQ-4bit --leash none
```

Keep this terminal running.

## Start the harness

Terminal 2, from the project directory:

```bash
lah
```

Read-only mode is the default. To enable Write, Edit, and Bash tools:

```bash
lah --write
```

Or toggle in a running session:

```text
/write on
/write off
```

## Commands

```text
/help
/new
/sessions
/resume SESSION_ID
/memory
/remember The API uses FastAPI and SQLAlchemy.
 /search FastAPI
/quit
```

## Persistence model

- Full chat transcript is stored in SQLite after each user turn.
- `/resume SESSION_ID` restores the saved `agent.messages`.
- `/remember TEXT` stores explicit long-term project memory.
- Memory is scoped to the resolved project path.
- SQLite is stored outside the repository in:
  `~/Library/Application Support/LocalAgentHarness/<project-key>/state.sqlite3`

This keeps agent memory even when mlx-code worktrees are cleaned up.

## Important implementation note

This MVP uses the documented `mlx_code.repl.Agent` API:
`Agent(system=..., tool_names=...)`, `agent.run(...)`, and `agent.messages`.

It intentionally keeps the transcript in SQLite rather than relying only on mlx-code's Git checkpoints.
Because the package is installed separately via `uv tool`, make sure the harness Python environment
can import `mlx_code`. If it cannot, install `mlx-code==0.0.42` in the harness venv or use the
same interpreter as the uv tool environment.

## Current limitations

- No automatic summarization/compaction yet.
- Long-term memory is explicitly saved with `/remember`.
- No multi-agent execution.
- No automatic approval prompt around individual shell commands; therefore write mode should be
  enabled only when you trust the task and the project. Read-only mode is the safe default.
- The runtime's worktree behavior should be tested on a disposable Git repository before using
  write mode on important projects.
